title: Why Stress Wipes Your Memory Clean: The Cortisol Connection
hook: Stress makes it harder to remember simple things, like where you left your keys.

narration.text: Stress makes it harder to remember simple things, like where you left your keys.
When you are stressed, your body releases a hormone called cortisol.
Cortisol is helpful for short-term danger, preparing you to act quickly.
However, high cortisol levels can interfere with brain areas vital for memory.
It especially affects the hippocampus, crucial for forming new memories.
This is why recalling recent events or learning new facts becomes a struggle.
So, reducing stress can actually help improve your memory function.
Have you noticed your memory getting worse when you are feeling stressed?

description: Ever wondered why your memory fails you under pressure? It turns out stress hormones play a big role. Discover how cortisol impacts your brain's ability to recall information and form new memories.
topic: Why stress can make it harder to remember things, explaining the role of cortisol.
